newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav farm output well below plan - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav farm output well below plan - analysts.

text.p: Yugoslavia's agricultural output will fall well below plan this year, and is unlikely to reach the government's target in 1997, analysts said on Wednesday.

"It is unlikely that agricultural output will rise by (the government's) targeted three percent this year," a source close to the federal agriculture ministry told Reuters on condition of anonymity. "The growth rate could even be negative."
The independent Institute for Market Research has estimated the sector's output this year will decline by four percent, pushed down by a poor wheat harvest.
According to figures supplied by the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce, agricultural output fell by 2.5 percent in the first nine months of the year, after growing three percent last year.
Agriculture was the key factor helping the Yugoslav economy endure four years of crippling international trade sanctions slapped on Belgrade for its involvement in the Bosnian war.
Experts said the government's expected five to six percent growth in agricultural output next year was unrealistic unless the farming sector received a strong increase in financial aid.
"The empty budget is the main problem," Miroslav Vidanovic of the Serbian ministry for development said.
Farmers had not yet been paid for this year's sunflower and sugarbeet harvest and many of them had threatened to hold up the spring sowing unless they received the funds, he added.
Milan Njegomir, director of the Yugoslav livestock fund, said the situation in the entire sector had never been worse.
"The government must come up with concrete measures and provide capital if it wants the proposed targets to be achieved," he said.
Officials at the federal ministry for agriculture dismissed the criticism and insisted the 1997 target was achievable, adding output levels depended to a large extent on the weather.
"Agriculture is like an open-air factory -- everything depends on the weather," a ministry official said.

The chamber of commerce estimates losses in agriculture topped 394 million dinars ($76.5) in the first half of the year, double the ammount in the same period of last year. In all of 1995 losses stood at 750 million dinars.
About 1,600 agricultural enterprises employing some 70,000 workers are insolvent and another 100 firms with about 5,000 employees each are in receivership, official figures show.
Average monthly wages in the agricultural sector stood at 377 dinars ($73) in the first six months, about 30 percent below the country's overall average.
Wheat production this year was 1.51 million tonnes, barely half the 2.97 million tonnes harvested in 1995 and compared with a forecast 1.7 million.
The Yugoslav maize crop has been estimated at 5.1 to 5.5 million tonnes, against 5.7 million last year.
